title: Towards Highly Compatible I/O-Aware Workflow Scheduling on HPC Systems
problem: Scientific workflows on HPC systems require efficient co-scheduling of computing and I/O resources, but existing solutions lack both co-scheduling capability and compatibility with traditional HPC batch schedulers.
motivation: Efficient resource scheduling across workflow tasks with dependencies is crucial for optimizing performance in large-scale HPC systems.
method: The paper introduces a performance model for workflow scheduling and proposes THman, an open-source scheduler implementing the Highest Contribution First (HCF) heuristic algorithm. THman performs online co-scheduling of computing and multi-tier storage resources while integrating with existing HPC batch schedulers for compatibility.
key_novelty: Online co-scheduling of computing and I/O resources integrated with traditional HPC batch schedulers for high compatibility.
contributions: Performance model for understanding workflow scheduling on HPC systems
THman open-source scientific workflow scheduler with online co-scheduling
Highest Contribution First (HCF) heuristic scheduling algorithm
30.9% makespan reduction demonstrated on simulated and real-world workloads
